newsitem.title: USA: IMF approves release of $15 mln for Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves release of $15 mln for Sierra Leone.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund Wednesday approved the release of $15 million in low-cost loans for war-torn Sierra Leone, monetary sources said.
"The economic reform program remains on track," one source, who declined to be named, said.

The money, which will be made available to the government before the middle of this month, is the second tranche of a three-year Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) loan first approved last year.
ESAF lends money at a half percent interest to the world's poorest nations to encourage them to reform their economies.
The IMF plans to send a mission to Sierra Leone next month to negotiate a reform program for next year, the sources said.

IMF board members on Tuesday encouraged Sierra Leone to press ahead with its reforms, particularly on the structural side, and to provide sufficient money for resettlement, rehabilitation and reconstruction.
They also called on the country to start cutting military spending, if conditions allow, the sources said.
The IMF warned Sierra Leone over the summer to reduce the wage bill for South African mercenaries helping the government fight rebels. The government subsequently did so.
